362|class MenuGroup:
363|    """One option group on one item, with the axis it belongs to."""
364|
365|    __slots__ = ("item_name", "group_name", "axis", "required", "min", "max",
366|                 "multiselect", "allows_quantity", "options", "_canonical")
367|
368|    def __init__(self, item_name: str, data: dict, config: mapping.Mapping):
369|        self.item_name = item_name
370|        self.group_name = data.get("group_name") or ""
371|        # The snapshot records an axis; the config can re-route a group the
372|        # capture didn't recognise, without re-fetching the menu.
373|        self.axis = config.axis_groups.get(self.group_name) or data.get("axis") or "other"
374|        self.min = data.get("min") or 0
375|        self.max = data.get("max")
376|        self.required = bool(data.get("required")) or self.min > 0
377|        self.multiselect = bool(data.get("multiselect"))
378|        self.allows_quantity = bool(data.get("allows_quantity"))
379|        self.options = [option for option in data.get("options") or []
380|                        if not option.get("is_disabled")]
381|        self._canonical = data.get("canonical")
382|
383|    @property
384|    def names(self) -> list[str]:
385|        return [option["name"] for option in self.options]
386|
387|    def option(self, name: str) -> dict | None:
388|        key = norm(name)
389|        for option in self.options:
390|            if norm(option["name"]) == key:
391|                return option
392|        return None
393|
394|    def canonical(self) -> dict[str, str]:
395|        """{store-level label -> the literal to post}.
396|
397|        Sizes carry a map from the capture ("Large" -> "Large .7"); sugar is
398|        keyed on its percentage, because the store's own wording is inconsistent
399|        English — `Regular Sugar 100%` beside `Less S 70%` (Task 1 §5). Every
400|        other axis already reads as itself.
401|        """
402|        if self.axis == "sugar":
403|            labels = {}
404|            for option in self.options:
405|                found = re.search(r"(\d+)\s*%", option["name"])
406|                labels[f"{found.group(1)}%" if found else option["name"]] = option["name"]
407|            return labels
408|        if isinstance(self._canonical, dict) and self._canonical:
409|            return self._canonical
410|        if self.axis != "size":
411|            return {name: name for name in self.names}
412|        return {size_label(option["name"], option.get("price")): option["name"]
413|                for option in self.options}
414|
415|    def label_for(self, option_name: str) -> str:
416|        """The literal back to its store-level label: "Less S 70%" -> "70%"."""
417|        for label, literal in self.canonical().items():
418|            if literal == option_name:
419|                return label
420|        return option_name
421|
422|    def default(self, prefer: list[str] | None = None) -> dict | None:
423|        """What to send when this group is required and nobody chose anything.
424|
425|        The menu's own default first, then whatever the mapping says this store
426|        normally serves, then the cheapest option — and never a "No ..." removal
427|        option if there is anything else, because a required group defaulting to
428|        "without" is the one guess that changes the drink.
429|        """
430|        for option in self.options:
431|            if option.get("is_default"):
432|                return option
433|        labels = self.canonical()
434|        for wanted in prefer or ():
435|            key = norm(wanted)
436|            for option in self.options:
437|                if norm(option["name"]) == key:
438|                    return option
439|            for label, literal in labels.items():
440|                if norm(label) == key:
441|                    return self.option(literal)
442|        positive = [option for option in self.options
443|                    if not norm(option["name"]).startswith("no ")] or self.options
444|        return min(positive, key=lambda option: (option.get("price") or 0),
445|                   default=None)

569|class StoreMenu:
570|    """Everything one store sells, indexed for lookup."""
571|
572|    def __init__(self, data: dict | None = None, config: mapping.Mapping | None = None):
573|        data = data or {}
574|        self.config = config or mapping.load()
575|        self.restaurant_id = data.get("restaurant_id") or ""
576|        self.store = data.get("restaurant_name") or (data.get("store") or {}).get("name") or ""
577|        self.items = [MenuItem(item, self.config) for item in data.get("items") or []]
578|        self._vocabulary: dict | None = None
579|
580|        excluded = tuple(word.lower() for word in self.config.drink_exclude)
581|        self.drinks = [item for item in self.items
582|                       if item.available
583|                       and not any(word in item.name.lower() for word in excluded)]
584|
585|        # Name -> item. Duplicates resolve to the lowest id so the same sheet
586|        # produces the same cart twice running (Task 1 §5).
587|        self._by_name: dict[str, MenuItem] = {}
588|        self._by_squash: dict[str, list[MenuItem]] = {}
589|        for item in sorted(self.drinks, key=lambda item: item.id):
590|            self._by_name.setdefault(norm(item.name), item)
591|            self._by_squash.setdefault(squash(item.name), []).append(item)
592|        self._aliases = {norm(key): value
593|                         for key, value in self.config.drink_aliases.items()}
594|        # Everything, including what's sold out and what we never order (gift
595|        # cards). Only used to tell someone *why* their drink isn't offered.
596|        self._any_by_name: dict[str, MenuItem] = {}
597|        for item in sorted(self.items, key=lambda item: item.id):
598|            self._any_by_name.setdefault(norm(item.name), item)
599|            self._any_by_name.setdefault(squash(item.name), item)
600|
601|    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
602|        return bool(self.items)
603|
604|    def __len__(self) -> int:
605|        return len(self.items)
606|
607|    @property
608|    def names(self) -> list[str]:
609|        seen: dict[str, None] = {}
610|        for item in self.drinks:
611|            seen.setdefault(item.name, None)
612|        return list(seen)
613|
614|    def by_id(self, item_id: str) -> MenuItem | None:
615|        return next((item for item in self.items if item.id == item_id), None)
616|
617|    def find(self, text: str) -> Match:
618|        """A drink name -> the item to order, and how sure we are.
619|
620|        Only three tiers get here, and all three are the *same name*: exactly as
621|        written, the same name spelled differently, or a name the mapping file
622|        says is this drink. Anything looser is a guess about what somebody wants
623|        to drink, and app/matcher.py offers those rather than applying them.
624|        """
625|        key = norm(text)
626|        if not key or not self.drinks:
627|            return Match()
628|
629|        exact = self._by_name.get(key)
630|        if exact:
631|            return Match(exact, Match.EXACT)
632|
633|        alias = self._aliases.get(key)
634|        if alias:
635|            target = self._by_name.get(norm(alias))
636|            if target:
637|                return Match(target, Match.ALIAS)
638|
639|        # "Wintermelon Lemonade" and "Winter Melon Lemonade" are one drink typed
640|        # two ways, not a judgement call — unless the squashed key hits two
641|        # genuinely different names, which would be.
642|        candidates = self._by_squash.get(squash(text)) or []
643|        distinct = {item.name for item in candidates}
644|        if len(distinct) == 1:
645|            return Match(candidates[0], Match.NORMALISED)
646|        if len(distinct) > 1:
647|            return Match(None, Match.AMBIGUOUS, sorted(distinct))
648|        return Match()
649|
650|    def vocabulary(self) -> dict:
651|        """Every label any drink here offers, per axis.
652|
653|        The fallback for a row whose drink nobody has picked yet: there is no
654|        item to ask, so the review screen offers what the store has and the
655|        match narrows it the moment a drink is chosen. Walks every item, so the
656|        answer is kept once it has been worked out.
657|        """
658|        if self._vocabulary is not None:
659|            return self._vocabulary
660|        found: dict[str, list[str]] = {axis: [] for axis in
661|                                       ("size", "sugar", "ice", "milk", "toppings")}
662|        for item in self.drinks:
663|            for axis, names in found.items():
664|                for name in (item.options(axis) if axis == "toppings"
665|                             else item.labels(axis)):
666|                    if name not in names:
667|                        names.append(name)
668|        found["sugar"].sort(key=lambda label: int(re.sub(r"\D", "", label) or 0))
669|        self._vocabulary = found
670|        return found
671|
672|    def unorderable(self, text: str) -> MenuItem | None:
673|        """An item this store lists but we won't order — sold out, or a gift card.
674|
675|        `find()` never returns these. This exists so the reason can be "Taro
676|        Slush is sold out today" instead of "no drink called Taro Slush".
677|        """
678|        if not text:
679|            return None
680|        item = self._any_by_name.get(norm(text)) or self._any_by_name.get(squash(text))
681|        if item is None or item in self.drinks:
682|            return None
683|        return item
684|
685|    def suggestions(self, text: str, limit: int = 5) -> list[str]:
686|        """Near misses to offer a person, best first. Never applied on our own."""
687|        key = norm(text)
688|        if not key or not self.drinks:
689|            return []
690|        wanted = {word for word in key.split() if len(word) >= 3}
691|        cutoff = self.config.drink_cutoff
692|        scored: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
693|        for name in self.names:
694|            candidate = norm(name)
695|            score = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, key, candidate).ratio()
696|            if wanted:
697|                shared = wanted & set(candidate.split())
698|                score = max(score, 0.9 * len(shared) / len(wanted))
699|            if score >= cutoff:
700|                scored.append((score, name))
701|        scored.sort(key=lambda pair: (-pair[0], pair[1]))
702|        return [name for _score, name in scored[:limit]]

84|def parse_multipart(body: bytes, content_type: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
85|    match = re.search(r'boundary="?([^";]+)"?', content_type or "")
86|    if not match:
87|        return {}
88|    boundary = b"--" + match.group(1).strip().encode()
89|
90|    fields: dict[str, dict] = {}
91|    for chunk in body.split(boundary):
92|        if chunk in (b"", b"--", b"--\r\n", b"\r\n"):
93|            continue
94|        chunk = chunk.lstrip(b"\r\n")
95|        head, _, payload = chunk.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
96|        if not _:
97|            continue
98|        payload = payload[:-2] if payload.endswith(b"\r\n") else payload
99|
100|        headers = head.decode("utf-8", "replace")
101|        name = re.search(r'name="([^"]*)"', headers)
102|        if not name:
103|            continue
104|        filename = re.search(r'filename="([^"]*)"', headers)
105|        fields[name.group(1)] = {
106|            "value": payload,
107|            "filename": filename.group(1) if filename else None,
108|        }
109|    return fields

84|def parse_multipart(body: bytes, content_type: str) -> dict[str, dict]:
85|    match = re.search(r'boundary="?([^";]+)"?', content_type or "")
86|    if not match:
87|        return {}
88|    boundary = b"--" + match.group(1).strip().encode()
89|
90|    fields: dict[str, dict] = {}
91|    for chunk in body.split(boundary):
92|        if chunk in (b"", b"--", b"--\r\n", b"\r\n"):
93|            continue
94|        chunk = chunk.lstrip(b"\r\n")
95|        head, _, payload = chunk.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
96|        if not _:
97|            continue
98|        payload = payload[:-2] if payload.endswith(b"\r\n") else payload
99|
100|        headers = head.decode("utf-8", "replace")
101|        name = re.search(r'name="([^"]*)"', headers)
102|        if not name:
103|            continue
104|        filename = re.search(r'filename="([^"]*)"', headers)
105|        fields[name.group(1)] = {
106|            "value": payload,
107|            "filename": filename.group(1) if filename else None,
108|        }
109|    return fields

Gathering organizer UI, index form, matcher pricing, group_orders tests, and docs to decide hard block vs soft warning and retroactive cap handling.

Need to also see organizer JS/html, index.html (creation form), matcher price data, tests for group_orders, docs task design notes for recent tasks to follow pattern.

Key decisions for Task 20:

From description:
- organizer option to set per-person budget when creating session
- participants understand limit before they build drink
- find out at selection time (not after submitting) if choice exceeds it
- Decide hard block vs soft warning
- How to handle multiple drinks — per drink or per person total?
- What happens to orders already submitted if organizer changes cap afterward.
- Requires price data, depends on prices being captured with menu.

So need to design:
- budget_cap field on room (dollars? cents?). Optional. Set at creation, updatable by organizer afterward.
- Per-person total interpretation seems most sensible for "maximum spend per person" — cap applies to person's running total (sum of estimated totals for all their order lines, case-insensitive name match). Need to decide: enforce on add/update.
- Hard block or soft warning? The task says "Decide whether the cap is a hard block or a soft warning". Need to pick one and document. Could do soft warning? But "enforced or warned on at order time" in Goal says enforced or warned. Simplest robust: hard block at order time (server rejects orders that would push person over cap) + live client warning at selection time. That satisfies both "enforced" and "find out at selection time". Alternatively soft warning: allow but flag. Need to choose. Hard block makes sense when organizer/team budget covering cost. Soft warning risks overspend. So hard block = better. But we should also support organizer override? Organizer token can bypass? That would be nice: organizer can manage any order and may need to allow exception. Let's think: if organizer edits, should bypass? Perhaps organizer override allowed. But spec doesn't say.

- What happens to orders already submitted if organizer changes cap afterward? Decision: existing orders are grandfathered (kept, flagged as over-budget in dashboard), new orders/edits must respect new cap. Never auto-delete. That is least surprising.

- Participant UX: show budget banner before building drink, live estimate vs cap at selection time (in updateEstimate), block submit client-side with clear message, server also enforces.

- Need price data: use matcher-estimated totals (same as costs). Server must compute prospective person's total.

Let's look at matcher to understand pricing, and organizer UI, creation UI, tests.
I've got the shape of the budget feature — now digging into pricing and the organizer controls.

1|"""Rows -> exact menu items and exact modifier strings. Task 4.
2|
3|    python3 -m app.matcher .runs/<id>.json
4|
5|`app/options.py` got the sheet as far as the store's own words: `Large`, `50%`,
6|`Boba`. That is as far as anything can get without knowing which drink it is,
7|because Kung Fu Tea defines its option groups per item (Task 1 §5) — `Large` is
8|`Large .7` on a Taro Slush, `Large 1` on the next drink along, and the upcharge
9|is part of the string. This module walks the second arrow:
10|
11|    "lg"  ->  "Large"  ->  "Large .7"  on this drink, in this group
12|              options.py   matcher.py
13|
14|and produces, for each row, a line the cart writer can post verbatim.
15|
16|WHAT IT DECIDES, AND WHAT IT REFUSES TO
17|---------------------------------------
18|It applies a drink name three ways, all of which are the *same name*: exactly as
19|written, the same name spelled differently ("Wintermelon Lemonade"), or an alias
20|from `data/mapping.json`. It will not pick between two drinks. A near miss comes
21|back as suggestions on the row and the preview asks a person, because every
22|other axis is a modifier costing pennies and the drink costs a whole drink.
23|
24|For modifiers it is the opposite: it decides, and says what it decided.
25|
26|* **not offered here** — "Large" on a drink sold in one size, `Espresso Shot` on
27|  a drink that doesn't take it. Reported with what that item *does* have, and
28|  dropped rather than guessed at — unless the group is required, where dropping
29|  it would only move the rejection to the store, so the item's own default goes
30|  in and the row says which and why.
31|* **already the default** — 31 Bay Ridge items have no `Regular Sugar 100%` and
32|  66 have no `Regular Ice`. Asking for those is not an impossible request, it is
33|  the recipe: send no modifier (Task 1 §5). Logged, not warned about.
34|* **required, and nobody said** — `Choose A Size` is `min 1` on 136 items and 9
35|  items must pick an included topping, so leaving them out is a rejected order,
36|  not a default. The item's own default is used, or the store's usual from the
37|  mapping file, and the row says so.
38|
39|Nothing here is fatal, and nothing here is silent. A row that can't be matched
40|still reaches the preview with its reasons attached, and the preview can fix any
41|of it in place — see `importer.apply_row_edit`.
42|"""

63|def _join(names, conjunction: str = "and", limit: int = 4) -> str:
64|    names = list(names)
65|    if not names:
66|        return "nothing"
67|    if len(names) > limit:
68|        return f"{', '.join(names[:limit])} and {len(names) - limit} more"
69|    if len(names) == 1:
70|        return names[0]
71|    return f"{', '.join(names[:-1])} {conjunction} {names[-1]}"

74|class Chosen:
75|    """One modifier's outcome on one item."""
76|
77|    __slots__ = ("group", "option", "axis", "asked", "quantity", "status",
78|                 "message", "choices")
79|
80|    OK = "ok"                  # asked for, and this item has it
81|    DEFAULTED = "defaulted"    # nobody asked; the group is required so we picked
82|    IS_DEFAULT = "is_default"  # asked for, and it's the recipe — send nothing
83|    NOT_HERE = "not_here"      # this item doesn't offer it
84|    NO_GROUP = "no_group"      # this item has no such axis at all
85|
86|    def __init__(self, axis: str, group=None, option: dict | None = None,
87|                 quantity: int = 1, status: str = OK, message: str = "",
88|                 choices: list[str] | None = None, asked: str = ""):
89|        self.axis = axis
90|        self.group = group
91|        self.option = option
92|        # What the row asked for, so the page can offer to replace exactly that
93|        # one — a row can ask for four toppings and only trip on the third.
94|        self.asked = asked
95|        self.quantity = quantity
96|        self.status = status
97|        self.message = message
98|        self.choices = choices or []
99|
100|    def as_option(self) -> dict | None:
101|        """The line-item entry, keyed the way the cart API addresses it.
102|
103|        Task 1 §6: options carry no ids. Both the group and the option are
104|        referenced by their exact display name, which is why the group travels
105|        with the option and not just the axis.
106|        """
107|        if not self.option or not self.group:
108|            return None
109|        return {
110|            "group": self.group.group_name,
111|            "axis": self.axis,
112|            "name": self.option["name"],
113|            "quantity": self.quantity,
114|            "price": round((self.option.get("price") or 0) * self.quantity, 2),
115|        }
116|
117|
118|#: How loudly to say each thing. Nothing the matcher finds is an error: the
119|#: import decided long ago which rows are unorderable, and a modifier this store
120|#: can't do is a drink somebody still gets.
121|_LEVEL = {Chosen.NOT_HERE: "warning", Chosen.NO_GROUP: "info",
122|          Chosen.IS_DEFAULT: "info", Chosen.DEFAULTED: "info"}
123|
124|#: "<drink> <this> — it's <what it has>". One per axis because "doesn't come in
125|#: Large" and "doesn't do 0% sugar" are both the plain way to say it.
126|_NOT_HERE = {
127|    "size": "doesn't come in {label}",
128|    "sugar": "doesn't do {label} sugar",
129|    "ice": "doesn't do {label}",
130|    "milk": "doesn't do a milk alternative",
131|    "toppings": "doesn't take {label}",
132|}

135|class RowMatcher:
136|    """One row against one menu. Split out so the rules read in one place."""
137|
138|    def __init__(self, store: menu_module.StoreMenu, config: mapping.Mapping,
139|                 columns: dict | None = None):
140|        self.store = store
141|        self.config = config
142|        # Which fields the sheet actually had a column for. A blank Size cell in
143|        # a sheet with a Size column is worth a word; a whole missing column was
144|        # already reported once at the top by the importer.
145|        self.columns = {key.lower() for key in (columns or {})}

149|    def find_item(self, row: dict) -> tuple[menu_module.MenuItem | None, str, list[str]]:
150|        """(item, how it was found, what to offer instead).
151|
152|        The already-resolved name first, then what the sheet said — so the same
153|        three tiers apply whether or not options.py got there first, and a row
154|        somebody corrected by hand looks up the name they picked.
155|        """
156|        canonical = (row.get("canonical") or {}).get("drink") or ""
157|        typed = row.get("drink") or ""
158|        chosen = any((issue.get("code") or "") == "edited:drink"
159|                     for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
160|
161|        for text in (canonical, typed):
162|            if not text:
163|                continue
164|            found = self.store.find(text)
165|            if found:
166|                return found.item, "chosen" if chosen else found.how, []
167|            if found.how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
168|                return None, found.how, found.choices
169|        return None, menu_module.Match.NONE, self.store.suggestions(typed)

172|
173|    def choose(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, axis: str, label: str) -> Chosen:
174|        """A canonical label -> the exact option on this item, or a reason why not."""
175|        groups = item.groups_for(axis)
176|        required = [group for group in groups if group.required]
177|
178|        if not groups:
179|            if label:
180|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP, asked=label,
181|                              message=f"{item.name} has no {_axis_word(axis)} choice, so "
182|                                      f"\"{label}\" wasn't sent")
183|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP)
184|
185|        if label:
186|            found = item.literal(axis, label)
187|            if found:
188|                group, option = found
189|                return Chosen(axis, group, option)
190|
191|            offered = item.labels(axis)
192|            phrase = _NOT_HERE.get(axis, "doesn't take {label}").format(label=label)
193|            fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
194|            if fallback:
195|                # The group is required, so "send nothing" isn't on the table —
196|                # a line missing a required group is a rejected line. Something
197|                # gets ordered and the row says loudly what and why.
198|                group, option = fallback
199|                instead = group.label_for(option["name"])
200|                rest = [name for name in offered if name != instead]
201|                message = (f"{item.name} {phrase} — it only comes {instead}, so that's "
202|                           f"what's ordered") if not rest else (
203|                    f"{item.name} {phrase} — ordered {instead} for now; it also does "
204|                    f"{_join(rest, 'or')}")
205|                return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE,
206|                              choices=offered, asked=label, message=message)
207|            if self._is_the_recipe(axis, label):
208|                # Task 1 §5: no Regular Ice option means regular ice is what you
209|                # get. Sending nothing is the correct order, not a compromise.
210|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.IS_DEFAULT,
211|                              message=f"{label.lower()} is how {item.name} comes — "
212|                                      f"no {_axis_word(axis)} sent")
213|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered, asked=label,
214|                          message=f"{item.name} {phrase} — it's {_join(offered, 'or')}")
215|
216|        fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
217|        if fallback:
218|            group, option = fallback
219|            asked = axis in self.columns
220|            return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
221|                          message=(f"no {_axis_word(axis)} on this row, so {item.name} "
222|                                   f"is ordered {group.label_for(option['name'])}")
223|                                  if asked else "")
224|        return Chosen(axis)
225|
226|    def _fallback(self, required: list, axis: str):
227|        """(group, option) for the first required group that can fill itself in."""
228|        for group in required:
229|            option = group.default(self.config.required_fallback.get(axis))
230|            if option is not None:
231|                return group, option
232|        return None
233|
234|    def _is_the_recipe(self, axis: str, label: str) -> bool:
235|        return label.lower() in self.config.assumed_defaults.get(axis, ())
236|
237|    def choose_toppings(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, row: dict) -> list[Chosen]:
238|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
239|        wanted = list(canonical.get("toppings") or [])
240|        counts = canonical.get("topping_quantities") or {}
241|        offered = item.options("toppings")
242|        chosen: list[Chosen] = []
243|
244|        for name in wanted:
245|            found = item.literal("toppings", name)
246|            if not found:
247|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered,
248|                                     asked=name,
249|                                     message=f"{item.name} doesn't take {name}"
250|                                             if offered else
251|                                             f"{item.name} doesn't take toppings at all"))
252|                continue
253|            group, option = found
254|            count = int(counts.get(name) or 1)
255|            if count > 1 and not group.allows_quantity:
256|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, 1,
257|                                     message=f"{item.name} only takes one {name}"))
258|                continue
259|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, count))
260|
261|        # An "Included Topping" group is min 1: the drink is defined by it, so a
262|        # sheet that didn't mention it still has to say something.
263|        for group in item.groups_for("toppings"):
264|            if not group.required:
265|                continue
266|            if any(pick.group is group for pick in chosen):
267|                continue
268|            option = group.default()
269|            if option is None:
270|                continue
271|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
272|                                 message=f"{item.name} comes with {option['name']}"))
273|        return chosen

277|    def run(self, row: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[Issue]]:
278|        number = row.get("row_number")
279|        issues: list[Issue] = []
280|
281|        def note(chosen: Chosen, field: str) -> None:
282|            level = _LEVEL.get(chosen.status)
283|            if level and chosen.message:
284|                issues.append(Issue(level, chosen.message, field, number,
285|                                    f"{PREFIX}{chosen.status}:{field}"))
286|
287|        if not row.get("ok", True):
288|            return {"status": SKIPPED}, issues
289|
290|        item, how, offer = self.find_item(row)
291|        if item is None:
292|            typed = (row.get("drink") or "").strip()
293|            gone = self.store.unorderable(typed)
294|            message = ""
295|            if how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
296|                message = f"\"{typed}\" is two different drinks here — {_join(offer, 'or')}"
297|            elif gone is not None:
298|                message = (f"{gone.name} is sold out today" if gone.sold_out
299|                           else f"{gone.name} isn't something this can order")
300|                offer = offer or self.store.suggestions(typed)
301|            elif not _already_said(row, "drink"):
302|                # options.py says "no drink called X — did you mean Y?" while
303|                # resolving the row. Saying it again in different words would
304|                # only make the preview look like two things went wrong.
305|                message = f"no drink called \"{typed}\" on this store's menu"
306|                if offer:
307|                    message += f" — did you mean {_join(offer[:2], 'or')}?"
308|            if message:
309|                issues.append(Issue("warning", message, "drink", number,
310|                                    f"{PREFIX}no-item"))
311|            return {"status": NEEDS_DRINK, "choices": {"drink": offer}}, issues
312|
313|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
314|        picks = [self.choose(item, "size", canonical.get("size") or ""),
315|                 self.choose(item, "sugar", canonical.get("sugar") or ""),
316|                 self.choose(item, "ice", canonical.get("ice") or ""),
317|                 self.choose(item, "milk", canonical.get("milk") or "")]
318|        for pick in picks:
319|            note(pick, pick.axis)
320|        toppings = self.choose_toppings(item, row)
321|        for pick in toppings:
322|            note(pick, "toppings")
323|        picks += toppings
324|
325|        line_options = [entry for entry in
326|                        (pick.as_option() for pick in picks) if entry]
327|        quantity = int(row.get("quantity") or 1)
328|        unit = float(item.base_price or 0)
329|        extras = round(sum(entry["price"] for entry in line_options), 2)
330|
331|        # Two different bad outcomes, and the page shows them differently: one
332|        # is a decision waiting to be made, the other is a request this drink
333|        # simply can't take, with nothing to choose between.
334|        unmapped = [{"axis": pick.axis, "asked": pick.asked, "why": pick.message}
335|                    for pick in picks if pick.status == Chosen.NOT_HERE]
336|        dropped = [{"axis": pick.axis, "asked": pick.asked, "why": pick.message}
337|                   for pick in picks if pick.status == Chosen.NO_GROUP and pick.asked]
338|        choices = {pick.axis: pick.choices for pick in picks if pick.choices}
339|
340|        return {
341|            "status": READY,
342|            "matched_by": how,
343|            "item": item.as_dict(),
344|            "price_tier": item.price_tier,
345|            "quantity": quantity,
346|            "options": line_options,
347|            "unit_price": round(unit, 2),
348|            "extras_price": extras,
349|            "total": round((unit + extras) * quantity, 2),
350|            "unmapped": unmapped,
351|            "dropped": dropped,
352|            "choices": choices,
353|            "available": self.available(item),
354|        }, issues

359|        `choices` is only the axes that went wrong. This is the whole list, so

361|        this drink rather than the store's vocabulary as a whole — the two are
362|        very different (a slush has no ice level at all).
363|        """
364|        return {
365|            "size": item.labels("size"),
366|            "sugar": item.labels("sugar"),
367|            "ice": item.labels("ice"),
368|            "milk": item.labels("milk"),

388|def match(run: dict, store: menu_module.StoreMenu | None = None) -> dict:
389|    """Add a menu match to every row of a saved import. The Task 4 stage.
390|
391|    Pure: it reads the run and the menu snapshot and returns a new run. Running
392|    it twice on the same input gives the same answer — its own notes are cleared
393|    first — so the preview can re-derive it on every read rather than storing a
394|    result that goes stale the moment somebody corrects a row.
395|    """
396|    # `is None`, not `or`: an empty menu is falsy and must stay the one we were
397|    # handed, so "there is no snapshot" is reported rather than papered over.
398|    restaurant_id = (run.get("source") or {}).get("restaurant_id")
399|    store = menu_module.store_menu(restaurant_id) if store is None else store
400|    config = store.config
401|    matcher = RowMatcher(store, config, run.get("column_map"))
402|
403|    result = dict(run)
404|    rows: list[dict] = []
405|    # Our own notes go first, so re-matching replaces them rather than stacking
406|    # them up. options.py's "N drinks didn't match by name" goes too: it is the
407|    # same fact counted without the menu in hand, and this stage recounts it.
408|    issues = [issue for issue in run.get("issues") or []
409|              if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)
410|              and issue.get("code") != "option:unmatched-drinks"]
411|
412|    if not store:
413|        rows = [dict(row, match={"status": SKIPPED}) for row in run.get("rows") or []]
414|        issues.append(Issue("warning", "there's no menu snapshot for this store, so "
415|                                       "nothing could be matched to it — run "
416|                                       "scripts/fetch_menu.py", None, None,
417|                            f"{PREFIX}no-menu").as_dict())
418|        result["rows"] = rows
419|        result["issues"] = issues
420|        result["match"] = {"ready": 0, "needs_drink": 0, "skipped": len(rows)}
421|        return result
422|
423|    ready = 0
424|    drinks = 0
425|    subtotal = 0.0
426|    for row in run.get("rows") or []:
427|        row = dict(row)
428|        row["issues"] = [issue for issue in row.get("issues") or []
429|                         if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)]
430|        found, row_issues = matcher.run(row)
431|        row["issues"] += [issue.as_dict() for issue in row_issues]
432|        row["match"] = found
433|        if found["status"] == READY:
434|            ready += 1
435|            drinks += found["quantity"]
436|            subtotal += found["total"]
437|        rows.append(row)
438|
439|    # A preview flag means "look at this row", not only "the drink name did not
440|    # match". Include parser warnings and requests this particular drink cannot
441|    # take, even when the remaining line is still safe to add to a cart.
442|    attention = sum(
443|        1 for row in rows
444|        if (row.get("match") or {}).get("status") != READY
445|        or any(issue.get("level") in ("warning", "error")
446|               for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
447|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("unmapped"))
448|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("dropped"))
449|    )
450|
451|    unmatched = sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == NEEDS_DRINK)
452|    if unmatched:
453|        issues.append(Issue(
454|            "warning",
455|            f"{unmatched} drink{'s' if unmatched != 1 else ''} still need"
456|            f"{'' if unmatched != 1 else 's'} picking from the menu before the cart "
457|            f"can be built", "drink", None, f"{PREFIX}unmatched").as_dict())
458|
459|    captured = menu_module.captured_at(store.restaurant_id)
460|    age = (_dt.date.today() - captured).days if captured else None
461|    if age is not None and age > config.menu_stale_days:
462|        # Task 1 §6: options are addressed by name, so a rename breaks the cart
463|        # quietly. An old snapshot is the one way this stage is wrong without
464|        # noticing.
465|        issues.append(Issue(
466|            "info", f"this menu was captured {age} days ago — re-run "
467|                    f"scripts/fetch_menu.py if the cart starts rejecting options",
468|            None, None, f"{PREFIX}stale-menu").as_dict())
469|
470|    result["rows"] = rows
471|    result["issues"] = issues
472|    result["match"] = {
473|        "store": store.store,
474|        "restaurant_id": store.restaurant_id,
475|        "menu_items": len(store.drinks),
476|        "menu_captured": captured.isoformat() if captured else None,
477|        # What the whole store offers, for a row whose drink isn't picked yet.
478|        # Once it is, the row's own `match.available` is the narrower truth.
479|        "vocabulary": store.vocabulary(),
480|        "ready": ready,
481|        "needs_drink": unmatched,
482|        "skipped": sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == SKIPPED),
483|        "needs_attention": attention,
484|        "drinks": drinks,
485|        "subtotal": round(subtotal, 2),

1|"""Rows -> exact menu items and exact modifier strings. Task 4.
2|
3|    python3 -m app.matcher .runs/<id>.json
4|
5|`app/options.py` got the sheet as far as the store's own words: `Large`, `50%`,
6|`Boba`. That is as far as anything can get without knowing which drink it is,
7|because Kung Fu Tea defines its option groups per item (Task 1 §5) — `Large` is
8|`Large .7` on a Taro Slush, `Large 1` on the next drink along, and the upcharge
9|is part of the string. This module walks the second arrow:
10|
11|    "lg"  ->  "Large"  ->  "Large .7"  on this drink, in this group
12|              options.py   matcher.py
13|
14|and produces, for each row, a line the cart writer can post verbatim.
15|
16|WHAT IT DECIDES, AND WHAT IT REFUSES TO
17|---------------------------------------
18|It applies a drink name three ways, all of which are the *same name*: exactly as
19|written, the same name spelled differently ("Wintermelon Lemonade"), or an alias
20|from `data/mapping.json`. It will not pick between two drinks. A near miss comes
21|back as suggestions on the row and the preview asks a person, because every
22|other axis is a modifier costing pennies and the drink costs a whole drink.
23|
24|For modifiers it is the opposite: it decides, and says what it decided.
25|
26|* **not offered here** — "Large" on a drink sold in one size, `Espresso Shot` on
27|  a drink that doesn't take it. Reported with what that item *does* have, and
28|  dropped rather than guessed at — unless the group is required, where dropping
29|  it would only move the rejection to the store, so the item's own default goes
30|  in and the row says which and why.
31|* **already the default** — 31 Bay Ridge items have no `Regular Sugar 100%` and
32|  66 have no `Regular Ice`. Asking for those is not an impossible request, it is
33|  the recipe: send no modifier (Task 1 §5). Logged, not warned about.
34|* **required, and nobody said** — `Choose A Size` is `min 1` on 136 items and 9
35|  items must pick an included topping, so leaving them out is a rejected order,
36|  not a default. The item's own default is used, or the store's usual from the
37|  mapping file, and the row says so.
38|
39|Nothing here is fatal, and nothing here is silent. A row that can't be matched
40|still reaches the preview with its reasons attached, and the preview can fix any
41|of it in place — see `importer.apply_row_edit`.
42|"""

44|from __future__ import annotations
45|
46|import datetime as _dt
47|import json
48|import sys

50|from . import costs, mapping, menu as menu_module
51|from .schema import Issue
52|
53|#: Row-level outcomes.
54|READY = "ready"            # a complete line, ready to post
55|NEEDS_DRINK = "needs_drink"  # we know nothing to order; a person must choose
56|SKIPPED = "skipped"        # the import already called this row unorderable
57|
58|#: Codes this module owns, so re-matching replaces its notes instead of stacking
59|#: them. Everything it writes starts with this prefix.
60|PREFIX = "match:"
61|
62|
63|def _join(names, conjunction: str = "and", limit: int = 4) -> str:
64|    names = list(names)
65|    if not names:
66|        return "nothing"
67|    if len(names) > limit:
68|        return f"{', '.join(names[:limit])} and {len(names) - limit} more"
69|    if len(names) == 1:
70|        return names[0]
71|    return f"{', '.join(names[:-1])} {conjunction} {names[-1]}"

74|class Chosen:
75|    """One modifier's outcome on one item."""
76|
77|    __slots__ = ("group", "option", "axis", "asked", "quantity", "status",
78|                 "message", "choices")
79|
80|    OK = "ok"                  # asked for, and this item has it
81|    DEFAULTED = "defaulted"    # nobody asked; the group is required so we picked
82|    IS_DEFAULT = "is_default"  # asked for, and it's the recipe — send nothing
83|    NOT_HERE = "not_here"      # this item doesn't offer it
84|    NO_GROUP = "no_group"      # this item has no such axis at all
85|
86|    def __init__(self, axis: str, group=None, option: dict | None = None,
87|                 quantity: int = 1, status: str = OK, message: str = "",
88|                 choices: list[str] | None = None, asked: str = ""):
89|        self.axis = axis
90|        self.group = group
91|        self.option = option
92|        # What the row asked for, so the page can offer to replace exactly that
93|        # one — a row can ask for four toppings and only trip on the third.
94|        self.asked = asked
95|        self.quantity = quantity
96|        self.status = status
97|        self.message = message
98|        self.choices = choices or []
99|
100|    def as_option(self) -> dict | None:
101|        """The line-item entry, keyed the way the cart API addresses it.
102|
103|        Task 1 §6: options carry no ids. Both the group and the option are
104|        referenced by their exact display name, which is why the group travels
105|        with the option and not just the axis.
106|        """
107|        if not self.option or not self.group:
108|            return None
109|        return {
110|            "group": self.group.group_name,
111|            "axis": self.axis,
112|            "name": self.option["name"],
113|            "quantity": self.quantity,
114|            "price": round((self.option.get("price") or 0) * self.quantity, 2),
115|        }
116|
117|
118|#: How loudly to say each thing. Nothing the matcher finds is an error: the
119|#: import decided long ago which rows are unorderable, and a modifier this store
120|#: can't do is a drink somebody still gets.
121|_LEVEL = {Chosen.NOT_HERE: "warning", Chosen.NO_GROUP: "info",
122|          Chosen.IS_DEFAULT: "info", Chosen.DEFAULTED: "info"}
123|
124|#: "<drink> <this> — it's <what it has>". One per axis because "doesn't come in
125|#: Large" and "doesn't do 0% sugar" are both the plain way to say it.
126|_NOT_HERE = {
127|    "size": "doesn't come in {label}",
128|    "sugar": "doesn't do {label} sugar",
129|    "ice": "doesn't do {label}",
130|    "milk": "doesn't do a milk alternative",
131|    "toppings": "doesn't take {label}",
132|}

135|class RowMatcher:
136|    """One row against one menu. Split out so the rules read in one place."""
137|
138|    def __init__(self, store: menu_module.StoreMenu, config: mapping.Mapping,
139|                 columns: dict | None = None):
140|        self.store = store
141|        self.config = config
142|        # Which fields the sheet actually had a column for. A blank Size cell in
143|        # a sheet with a Size column is worth a word; a whole missing column was
144|        # already reported once at the top by the importer.
145|        self.columns = {key.lower() for key in (columns or {})}
146|
147|    # -- the drink ------------------------------------------------------------
148|
149|    def find_item(self, row: dict) -> tuple[menu_module.MenuItem | None, str, list[str]]:
150|        """(item, how it was found, what to offer instead).
151|
152|        The already-resolved name first, then what the sheet said — so the same
153|        three tiers apply whether or not options.py got there first, and a row
154|        somebody corrected by hand looks up the name they picked.
155|        """
156|        canonical = (row.get("canonical") or {}).get("drink") or ""
157|        typed = row.get("drink") or ""
158|        chosen = any((issue.get("code") or "") == "edited:drink"
159|                     for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
160|
161|        for text in (canonical, typed):
162|            if not text:
163|                continue
164|            found = self.store.find(text)
165|            if found:
166|                return found.item, "chosen" if chosen else found.how, []
167|            if found.how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
168|                return None, found.how, found.choices
169|        return None, menu_module.Match.NONE, self.store.suggestions(typed)
170|
171|    # -- the modifiers --------------------------------------------------------
172|
173|    def choose(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, axis: str, label: str) -> Chosen:
174|        """A canonical label -> the exact option on this item, or a reason why not."""
175|        groups = item.groups_for(axis)
176|        required = [group for group in groups if group.required]
177|
178|        if not groups:
179|            if label:
180|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP, asked=label,
181|                              message=f"{item.name} has no {_axis_word(axis)} choice, so "
182|                                      f"\"{label}\" wasn't sent")
183|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NO_GROUP)
184|
185|        if label:
186|            found = item.literal(axis, label)
187|            if found:
188|                group, option = found
189|                return Chosen(axis, group, option)
190|
191|            offered = item.labels(axis)
192|            phrase = _NOT_HERE.get(axis, "doesn't take {label}").format(label=label)
193|            fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
194|            if fallback:
195|                # The group is required, so "send nothing" isn't on the table —
196|                # a line missing a required group is a rejected line. Something
197|                # gets ordered and the row says loudly what and why.
198|                group, option = fallback
199|                instead = group.label_for(option["name"])
200|                rest = [name for name in offered if name != instead]
201|                message = (f"{item.name} {phrase} — it only comes {instead}, so that's "
202|                           f"what's ordered") if not rest else (
203|                    f"{item.name} {phrase} — ordered {instead} for now; it also does "
204|                    f"{_join(rest, 'or')}")
205|                return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE,
206|                              choices=offered, asked=label, message=message)
207|            if self._is_the_recipe(axis, label):
208|                # Task 1 §5: no Regular Ice option means regular ice is what you
209|                # get. Sending nothing is the correct order, not a compromise.
210|                return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.IS_DEFAULT,
211|                              message=f"{label.lower()} is how {item.name} comes — "
212|                                      f"no {_axis_word(axis)} sent")
213|            return Chosen(axis, status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered, asked=label,
214|                          message=f"{item.name} {phrase} — it's {_join(offered, 'or')}")
215|
216|        fallback = self._fallback(required, axis)
217|        if fallback:
218|            group, option = fallback
219|            asked = axis in self.columns
220|            return Chosen(axis, group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
221|                          message=(f"no {_axis_word(axis)} on this row, so {item.name} "
222|                                   f"is ordered {group.label_for(option['name'])}")
223|                                  if asked else "")
224|        return Chosen(axis)
225|
226|    def _fallback(self, required: list, axis: str):
227|        """(group, option) for the first required group that can fill itself in."""
228|        for group in required:
229|            option = group.default(self.config.required_fallback.get(axis))
230|            if option is not None:
231|                return group, option
232|        return None
233|
234|    def _is_the_recipe(self, axis: str, label: str) -> bool:
235|        return label.lower() in self.config.assumed_defaults.get(axis, ())
236|
237|    def choose_toppings(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem, row: dict) -> list[Chosen]:
238|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
239|        wanted = list(canonical.get("toppings") or [])
240|        counts = canonical.get("topping_quantities") or {}
241|        offered = item.options("toppings")
242|        chosen: list[Chosen] = []
243|
244|        for name in wanted:
245|            found = item.literal("toppings", name)
246|            if not found:
247|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", status=Chosen.NOT_HERE, choices=offered,
248|                                     asked=name,
249|                                     message=f"{item.name} doesn't take {name}"
250|                                             if offered else
251|                                             f"{item.name} doesn't take toppings at all"))
252|                continue
253|            group, option = found
254|            count = int(counts.get(name) or 1)
255|            if count > 1 and not group.allows_quantity:
256|                chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, 1,
257|                                     message=f"{item.name} only takes one {name}"))
258|                continue
259|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, count))
260|
261|        # An "Included Topping" group is min 1: the drink is defined by it, so a
262|        # sheet that didn't mention it still has to say something.
263|        for group in item.groups_for("toppings"):
264|            if not group.required:
265|                continue
266|            if any(pick.group is group for pick in chosen):
267|                continue
268|            option = group.default()
269|            if option is None:
270|                continue
271|            chosen.append(Chosen("toppings", group, option, status=Chosen.DEFAULTED,
272|                                 message=f"{item.name} comes with {option['name']}"))
273|        return chosen
274|
275|    # -- the row --------------------------------------------------------------
276|
277|    def run(self, row: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[Issue]]:
278|        number = row.get("row_number")
279|        issues: list[Issue] = []
280|
281|        def note(chosen: Chosen, field: str) -> None:
282|            level = _LEVEL.get(chosen.status)
283|            if level and chosen.message:
284|                issues.append(Issue(level, chosen.message, field, number,
285|                                    f"{PREFIX}{chosen.status}:{field}"))
286|
287|        if not row.get("ok", True):
288|            return {"status": SKIPPED}, issues
289|
290|        item, how, offer = self.find_item(row)
291|        if item is None:
292|            typed = (row.get("drink") or "").strip()
293|            gone = self.store.unorderable(typed)
294|            message = ""
295|            if how == menu_module.Match.AMBIGUOUS:
296|                message = f"\"{typed}\" is two different drinks here — {_join(offer, 'or')}"
297|            elif gone is not None:
298|                message = (f"{gone.name} is sold out today" if gone.sold_out
299|                           else f"{gone.name} isn't something this can order")
300|                offer = offer or self.store.suggestions(typed)
301|            elif not _already_said(row, "drink"):
302|                # options.py says "no drink called X — did you mean Y?" while
303|                # resolving the row. Saying it again in different words would
304|                # only make the preview look like two things went wrong.
305|                message = f"no drink called \"{typed}\" on this store's menu"
306|                if offer:
307|                    message += f" — did you mean {_join(offer[:2], 'or')}?"
308|            if message:
309|                issues.append(Issue("warning", message, "drink", number,
310|                                    f"{PREFIX}no-item"))
311|            return {"status": NEEDS_DRINK, "choices": {"drink": offer}}, issues
312|
313|        canonical = row.get("canonical") or {}
314|        picks = [self.choose(item, "size", canonical.get("size") or ""),
315|                 self.choose(item, "sugar", canonical.get("sugar") or ""),
316|                 self.choose(item, "ice", canonical.get("ice") or ""),
317|                 self.choose(item, "milk", canonical.get("milk") or "")]
318|        for pick in picks:
319|            note(pick, pick.axis)
320|        toppings = self.choose_toppings(item, row)
321|        for pick in toppings:
322|            note(pick, "toppings")
323|        picks += toppings
324|
325|        line_options = [entry for entry in
326|                        (pick.as_option() for pick in picks) if entry]
327|        quantity = int(row.get("quantity") or 1)
328|        unit = float(item.base_price or 0)
329|        extras = round(sum(entry["price"] for entry in line_options), 2)
330|
331|        # Two different bad outcomes, and the page shows them differently: one
332|        # is a decision waiting to be made, the other is a request this drink
333|        # simply can't take, with nothing to choose between.
334|        unmapped = [{"axis": pick.axis, "asked": pick.asked, "why": pick.message}
335|                    for pick in picks if pick.status == Chosen.NOT_HERE]
336|        dropped = [{"axis": pick.axis, "asked": pick.asked, "why": pick.message}
337|                   for pick in picks if pick.status == Chosen.NO_GROUP and pick.asked]
338|        choices = {pick.axis: pick.choices for pick in picks if pick.choices}
339|
340|        return {
341|            "status": READY,
342|            "matched_by": how,
343|            "item": item.as_dict(),
344|            "price_tier": item.price_tier,
345|            "quantity": quantity,
346|            "options": line_options,
347|            "unit_price": round(unit, 2),
348|            "extras_price": extras,
349|            "total": round((unit + extras) * quantity, 2),
350|            "unmapped": unmapped,
351|            "dropped": dropped,
352|            "choices": choices,
353|            "available": self.available(item),
354|        }, issues

356|    def available(self, item: menu_module.MenuItem) -> dict:
357|        """Everything this one drink can be ordered with, per axis.
358|
359|        `choices` is only the axes that went wrong. This is the whole list, so
360|        the review screen can offer a dropdown of what is actually possible for
361|        this drink rather than the store's vocabulary as a whole — the two are
362|        very different (a slush has no ice level at all).
363|        """

365|            "size": item.labels("size"),
366|            "sugar": item.labels("sugar"),
367|            "ice": item.labels("ice"),
368|            "milk": item.labels("milk"),
369|            "toppings": item.options("toppings"),

388|def match(run: dict, store: menu_module.StoreMenu | None = None) -> dict:
389|    """Add a menu match to every row of a saved import. The Task 4 stage.
390|
391|    Pure: it reads the run and the menu snapshot and returns a new run. Running
392|    it twice on the same input gives the same answer — its own notes are cleared
393|    first — so the preview can re-derive it on every read rather than storing a
394|    result that goes stale the moment somebody corrects a row.
395|    """
396|    # `is None`, not `or`: an empty menu is falsy and must stay the one we were
397|    # handed, so "there is no snapshot" is reported rather than papered over.
398|    restaurant_id = (run.get("source") or {}).get("restaurant_id")
399|    store = menu_module.store_menu(restaurant_id) if store is None else store
400|    config = store.config
401|    matcher = RowMatcher(store, config, run.get("column_map"))
402|
403|    result = dict(run)
404|    rows: list[dict] = []
405|    # Our own notes go first, so re-matching replaces them rather than stacking
406|    # them up. options.py's "N drinks didn't match by name" goes too: it is the
407|    # same fact counted without the menu in hand, and this stage recounts it.
408|    issues = [issue for issue in run.get("issues") or []
409|              if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)
410|              and issue.get("code") != "option:unmatched-drinks"]
411|
412|    if not store:
413|        rows = [dict(row, match={"status": SKIPPED}) for row in run.get("rows") or []]
414|        issues.append(Issue("warning", "there's no menu snapshot for this store, so "
415|                                       "nothing could be matched to it — run "
416|                                       "scripts/fetch_menu.py", None, None,
417|                            f"{PREFIX}no-menu").as_dict())
418|        result["rows"] = rows
419|        result["issues"] = issues
420|        result["match"] = {"ready": 0, "needs_drink": 0, "skipped": len(rows)}
421|        return result
422|
423|    ready = 0
424|    drinks = 0
425|    subtotal = 0.0
426|    for row in run.get("rows") or []:
427|        row = dict(row)
428|        row["issues"] = [issue for issue in row.get("issues") or []
429|                         if not str(issue.get("code") or "").startswith(PREFIX)]
430|        found, row_issues = matcher.run(row)
431|        row["issues"] += [issue.as_dict() for issue in row_issues]
432|        row["match"] = found
433|        if found["status"] == READY:
434|            ready += 1
435|            drinks += found["quantity"]
436|            subtotal += found["total"]
437|        rows.append(row)

439|    # A preview flag means "look at this row", not only "the drink name did not
440|    # match". Include parser warnings and requests this particular drink cannot
441|    # take, even when the remaining line is still safe to add to a cart.
442|    attention = sum(
443|        1 for row in rows
444|        if (row.get("match") or {}).get("status") != READY
445|        or any(issue.get("level") in ("warning", "error")
446|               for issue in row.get("issues") or [])
447|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("unmapped"))
448|        or bool((row.get("match") or {}).get("dropped"))
449|    )
450|
451|    unmatched = sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == NEEDS_DRINK)
452|    if unmatched:
453|        issues.append(Issue(
454|            "warning",
455|            f"{unmatched} drink{'s' if unmatched != 1 else ''} still need"
456|            f"{'' if unmatched != 1 else 's'} picking from the menu before the cart "
457|            f"can be built", "drink", None, f"{PREFIX}unmatched").as_dict())
458|
459|    captured = menu_module.captured_at(store.restaurant_id)
460|    age = (_dt.date.today() - captured).days if captured else None
461|    if age is not None and age > config.menu_stale_days:
462|        # Task 1 §6: options are addressed by name, so a rename breaks the cart
463|        # quietly. An old snapshot is the one way this stage is wrong without
464|        # noticing.
465|        issues.append(Issue(
466|            "info", f"this menu was captured {age} days ago — re-run "
467|                    f"scripts/fetch_menu.py if the cart starts rejecting options",
468|            None, None, f"{PREFIX}stale-menu").as_dict())
469|
470|    result["rows"] = rows
471|    result["issues"] = issues
472|    result["match"] = {
473|        "store": store.store,
474|        "restaurant_id": store.restaurant_id,
475|        "menu_items": len(store.drinks),
476|        "menu_captured": captured.isoformat() if captured else None,
477|        # What the whole store offers, for a row whose drink isn't picked yet.
478|        # Once it is, the row's own `match.available` is the narrower truth.
479|        "vocabulary": store.vocabulary(),
480|        "ready": ready,
481|        "needs_drink": unmatched,
482|        "skipped": sum(1 for row in rows if row["match"]["status"] == SKIPPED),
483|        "needs_attention": attention,
484|        "drinks": drinks,
485|        "subtotal": round(subtotal, 2),

489|                       else costs.from_rows(rows))

Reviewing app and test flows while designing a hard-block budget cap using the existing matcher pipeline for prospective order pricing.

Also need to check app.js creation flow, group-order.js end, docs for previous tasks to understand design doc conventions, and check status board tests, costs tests.

Also need to check how prices computed for prospective order before submit: participant JS already computes estimate locally (updateEstimate). Server enforcement needs to price prospective order using same matcher pipeline.

Design:

Backend:
- room fields: budget_cap (float dollars or None), budget_updated_at? Maybe budget_mode? Task says "Decide whether the cap is a hard block or a soft warning" — I decide hard block. So no mode needed, or include mode but default hard? Simpler: hard block enforced server-side, with client-side live warning before submit. Document decision in docs/task20-budget-cap.md. Could also add "warn-only" toggle? Task says "Decide whether..." implying pick one. Keep it simple: hard block. But maybe support both via flag? The request: "Decide whether the cap is a hard block or a soft warning, and how to handle people ordering multiple drinks — does the cap apply per drink or per person in total? Also decide what happens to orders already submitted if the organizer changes the cap afterward."

So decisions:
1. Hard block (not soft warning) — server rejects with 409 + code budget_exceeded; client shows at selection time and blocks submit. Rationale: organizer covering cost needs guarantee.
2. Cap applies per person in total (sum of all their drinks' estimated totals), not per drink. Rationale: "maximum spend per person" — multiple drinks count together; per-drink would let someone order 5 cheap drinks exceeding intent. Names grouped case-insensitively, same as aggregation.
3. Changing cap never removes/alters existing orders; they are grandfathered and flagged as over-budget in organizer view (and costs breakdown?). New adds/edits must fit new cap. Lowering cap doesn't invalidate old lines; raising cap unblocks new ones.

Implementation details:

- _clean_budget_cap(value): None/"" => None (no cap). Otherwise number (int/float or numeric string), finite, >0, upper bound? e.g., max $500? Let's set reasonable: >0 and <= 1000? Or MAX 9999? Look at price ranges: drinks ~ $5-8. Per-person cap maybe $5-50. Upper bound prevents nonsense but shouldn't be too strict. Use: must be number, 1..500? Let's use >0 and <= 1000. Round to cents (2 decimals). Return float rounded to 2.

- create(..., budget_cap=None): store room["budget_cap"] = cleaned or None. Include in public_room output: "budget_cap": room.get("budget_cap"). Also need per-person budget status? Provide budget info in public_room: for each person? Or let client compute? Better: public_room includes budget_cap and per-order estimated_total already; client can compute person's current total from session.orders + costs. But to help client show "you've spent X of $Y", include "budget" object? Keep simple: expose budget_cap, and also expose per-person totals via costs.by_person and summary. Client computes current person's total by matching name case-insensitively against orders' estimated_total.

But server enforcement must compute prospective total: price the new/updated order's line, sum with person's other lines (excluding the line being updated). Need helper _estimate_order_total(values, restaurant_id) -> float|None. Use importer+matcher same as _price_orders but for single row. If unpriced (needs_drink / skipped), then can't enforce — allow through (unpriced drinks not counted toward cap? Or block?). Decision: unpriced lines can't be checked, so they are allowed but flagged; cap only applies to priced lines. Document. Alternatively block unknown drinks? No — that would break when menu matching fails. Better to allow unpriced but they show as unpriced and organizer sees them. However that could be exploited to bypass cap with typo'd drink. But matcher will price most real drinks; typos need fixing anyway. Allowing is friendlier. Need to decide and document: unpriced lines are exempt from cap check (can't enforce without price), shown as unpriced.

Wait: _price_orders prices via matcher; estimated_total None when not READY. So enforcement: compute new line total; if None => allow. Else sum person's other priced totals + new total; if sum > cap + epsilon (1e-9? cents tolerance), reject.

Epsilon: use cents comparison to avoid float issues: convert to cents via round(total*100). If person_cents > cap_cents => reject.

Error type: new exception BudgetExceeded(RoomNotOpen? or GroupOrderError)? Should be 409 with code "budget_exceeded". Let's create class BudgetExceeded(GroupOrderError): status=409, code="budget_exceeded". Message includes cap and prospective total: e.g., "that would bring Alice to $X, over the $Y per-person limit".

Who is exempt? Organizer token managing any order — should organizer be able to override? If organizer edits via organizer_token, maybe allow over-cap? Hmm. If hard block, organizer covering budget might still want to allow exception for someone. But then organizer could just raise cap. 1|# Task 14 — Order Deadline & Countdown
2|
3|Every group order has an organizer-selected deadline. The creation form uses a
4|local `datetime-local` control (defaulting to roughly two hours ahead), converts
5|that choice to an ISO 8601 instant, and allows a cutoff no more than seven days
6|away. The server returns both `deadline_at` and `server_now`; countdowns use the
7|offset between those values and the browser clock so a mis-set participant
8|clock does not decide whether ordering is open.
9|
10|## Automatic locking
11|
12|The persisted room remains `open`, but its effective public status becomes
13|`locked` at the deadline with `lock_reason: "deadline"`,
14|`deadline_passed: true`, and `accepting_orders: false`. Every add, edit, and
15|participant delete checks the deadline again while holding the room lock, so a
16|stale page cannot submit late. Those requests return HTTP 409 with code
17|`deadline_passed`. Organizer moderation and finalization remain available.
18|
19|Participant and organizer pages update their countdown once per second and
20|switch immediately to the locked presentation at zero, then refresh from the
21|server. Participants keep the submitted-order list but lose the order editor;
22|the message tells late arrivals to contact the organizer.
23|
24|## Organizer controls
25|
26|The dashboard shows the countdown and exact local cutoff prominently. The
27|organizer can enter a new local date/time or extend by 15, 30, or 60 minutes.
28|It calls:
29|
30|`PATCH /api/group-orders/<room_id>/deadline`
31|
32|```json
33|{"deadline_at": "2026-09-10T19:30:00Z"}
34|```
35|
36|The organizer token is required. Moving an elapsed deadline into the future
37|reopens its automatic lock. Changing a deadline never clears a manual pause;
38|the organizer must explicitly reopen that room. A finalized or otherwise
39|permanently closed room cannot have its deadline changed.
40|
41|`expires_at` remains in the response as a compatibility alias for clients and
42|saved rooms from Task 8; new clients use `deadline_at`.

1|# Task 14 — Order Deadline & Countdown
2|
3|Every group order has an organizer-selected deadline. The creation form uses a
4|local `datetime-local` control (defaulting to roughly two hours ahead), converts
5|that choice to an ISO 8601 instant, and allows a cutoff no more than seven days
6|away. The server returns both `deadline_at` and `server_now`; countdowns use the
7|offset between those values and the browser clock so a mis-set participant
8|clock does not decide whether ordering is open.
9|
10|## Automatic locking
11|
12|The persisted room remains `open`, but its effective public status becomes
13|`locked` at the deadline with `lock_reason: "deadline"`,
14|`deadline_passed: true`, and `accepting_orders: false`. Every add, edit, and
15|participant delete checks the deadline again while holding the room lock, so a
16|stale page cannot submit late. Those requests return HTTP 409 with code
17|`deadline_passed`. Organizer moderation and finalization remain available.
18|
19|Participant and organizer pages update their countdown once per second and
20|switch immediately to the locked presentation at zero, then refresh from the
21|server. Participants keep the submitted-order list but lose the order editor;
22|the message tells late arrivals to contact the organizer.
23|
24|## Organizer controls
25|
26|The dashboard shows the countdown and exact local cutoff prominently. The
27|organizer can enter a new local date/time or extend by 15, 30, or 60 minutes.
28|It calls:
29|
30|`PATCH /api/group-orders/<room_id>/deadline`
31|
32|```json
33|{"deadline_at": "2026-09-10T19:30:00Z"}
34|```
35|
36|The organizer token is required. Moving an elapsed deadline into the future
37|reopens its automatic lock. Changing a deadline never clears a manual pause;
38|the organizer must explicitly reopen that room. A finalized or otherwise
39|permanently closed room cannot have its deadline changed.
40|
41|`expires_at` remains in the response as a compatibility alias for clients and
42|saved rooms from Task 8; new clients use `deadline_at`.

def _money_cents(value) -> int:
    return int(round(float(value or 0) * 100))


def _person_total(priced_orders: list[dict], person: str) -> float:
    """One person's priced total across already-priced lines.

    Names group case-insensitively, the same rule as the room summary, so
    "alice" and "Alice" share one cap. Unpriced lines (a drink the menu could
    not match) carry no amount and are excluded — without a price there is
    nothing to enforce, and Task 13 already reports those lines as unpriced.
    """
    key = (person or "").casefold()
    return round(sum(

        for order in priced_orders
        if (order.get("person") or "").casefold() == key
        and order.get("estimated_total") is not None
    ), 2)


def _check_budget(room: dict, values: dict, *, exclude_order_id: str | None = None,
                 organizer_override: bool = False,
                 current_total: float | None = None) -> None:
    """Reject a prospective order line that breaks the room's per-person cap.

    The cap applies to each person's total across all of their drinks — not
    per drink — because "maximum spend per person" is about what the organizer
    covers for that person. Pricing comes from the room's pinned captured menu
    via the matcher, never from client input.

    An organizer-token edit bypasses the check: it is the explicit override
    for exceptions and for fixing a line that is already over a lowered cap.
    A participant edit to a person who is already over (grandfathered when the
    organizer lowered the cap) is still allowed when it does not increase that
    person's total, so those lines are never frozen in place.
    """
    cap = room.get("budget_cap")
    if cap is None or organizer_override:
        return
    restaurant_id = room.get("restaurant_id") or menu.TARGET_STORE
    candidate = [order for order in room.get("orders") or []
                 if order.get("id") != exclude_order_id]
    probe = {
        "id": "__budget_probe__",
        "person": values["person"],
        "drink": values["drink"],
        "size": values.get("size", ""),
        "sugar": values.get("sugar", ""),
        "ice": values.get("ice", ""),
        "milk": values.get("milk", ""),
        "temperature": values.get("temperature", ""),
        "notes": values.get("notes", ""),
        "toppings": list(values.get("toppings") or []),
        "quantity": values.get("quantity", 1),
    }
    candidate.append(probe)
    priced, _costs = _price_orders(candidate, restaurant_id)
    probe_priced = priced[-1] if priced else {}
    if probe_priced.get("estimated_total") is None:
        return
    total = _person_total(priced, values["person"])
    if _money_cents(total) <= _money_cents(cap):

    if (current_total is not None

            and _money_cents(total) <= _money_cents(current_total)):
        return
    raise BudgetExceeded(
        f"{values['person']} would reach ${total:.2f}, "
        f"over the ${float(cap):.2f} per-person limit")

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.

</skill-body>

    group_orders.add_order(room["id"], {**ORDER, "drink": "Matcha Milk"})
    print("SECOND ADDED (unexpected?)")
except group_orders.BudgetExceeded as e:
    print("blocked:", e, e.code, e.status)
# different person ok
o2, t2, agg = group_orders.add_order(room["id"], {**ORDER, "person": "Bob"})
print("bob ok")
# case-insensitive
try:
    group_orders.add_order(room["id"], {**ORDER, "person": "ALICE"})
    print("ALICE ADDED (unexpected)")
except group_orders.BudgetExceeded as e:
    print("alice-case blocked:", e)
# unpriced allowed
o3, t3, agg = group_orders.add_order(room["id"], {**ORDER, "person": "Alice", "drink": "Zzz Not A Drink"})

# participant edit increasing blocked; organizer override allowed
try:
    group_orders.update_order(room["id"], o1["id"], {"quantity": 2}, order_token=t1)

except group_orders.BudgetExceeded as e:

upd, agg = group_orders.update_order(room["id"], o1["id"], {"quantity": 2}, organizer_token=tok)

# lower cap grandfathers

        group_orders.create(budget_cap=bad)
        print("ACCEPTED (bad):", bad)
    except group_orders.GroupOrderError as e:
        print("rejected:", repr(bad), "->", e)
